title: Qt: more dynamic menus to allow submenus beside Tools
description:
This is the result of the Issue discussion, to allow submenus for more dynamic menus such as Statistics or Telephony.

According to the comments in the source code, it is not possible to add menu items under Analyze from LUA, it also goes under Statistics.

Fix #20322 


Test lua plugin:

```lua
-- Define the menu entry's callback
local function dialog_menu()
    local function dialog_func(person,eyes,hair)
        local window = TextWindow.new("Person Info");
        local message = string.format("Person %s with %s eyes and %s hair.", person, eyes, hair);
        window:set(message);
    end

    new_dialog("Dialog Test",dialog_func,"A Person","Eyes","Hair")
end

-- Create the menu entry
register_menu("Test Analyze",   dialog_menu, MENU_PACKET_ANALYZE_UNSORTED) -- menu:Analyze[]
register_menu("Test Telephony", dialog_menu, MENU_TELEPHONY_UNSORTED)      -- menu:Telephony[]
register_menu("Test Packet",    dialog_menu, MENU_PACKET_STAT_UNSORTED)    -- menu:Statistics[]
register_menu("Test Tools",     dialog_menu, MENU_TOOLS_UNSORTED)          -- menu:Tools[]
register_menu("Test Generic",   dialog_menu, MENU_STAT_GENERIC)            -- menu:Statistics[], first section

register_menu("Test Analyze Sub/Lua Dialog Test1",   dialog_menu, MENU_PACKET_ANALYZE_UNSORTED) -- menu:Analyze[]
register_menu("Test Telephony Sub/Lua Dialog Test2", dialog_menu, MENU_TELEPHONY_UNSORTED)      -- menu:Telephony[]
register_menu("Test Packet Sub/Lua Dialog Test3",    dialog_menu, MENU_PACKET_STAT_UNSORTED)    -- menu:Statistics[]
register_menu("Test Tools Sub/Lua Dialog Test4",     dialog_menu, MENU_TOOLS_UNSORTED)          -- menu:Tools[]
```

mentioned in issue #20322

I don't completely love this approach, where in this case the menu is appended to the end and then a subsequent `insertMenu` moves it to the previous position. [This documentation](https://doc.qt.io/qt-6/qmenu.html#qmenu-on-macos-with-qt-build-against-cocoa) suggests that on MacOS this may not necessarily work. (It works fine on Linux and Windows, but I don't have a Mac.) For this case, it may be necessary to create the menu via its constructor and then insert it rather than using the `addMenu()` convenience function.

Please consider the current logic. I deliberately followed that to make sure it works the same way as of now.

You can see that in the switch case it's `addAction(action)` everywhere which I kept with my `addMenusandSubmenus` too.

When it comes to `REGISTER_STAT_GROUP_GENERIC`, it uses `insertMenu` within `main_ui_->menuStatistics` and it makes sure we add element above `actionStatistics_REGISTER_STAT_GROUP_UNSORTED`.

I have implemented the same logic.

So your concern should be valid for the current implementation too, right?

Could we take that separately please?

No, it's not the same. With the action, the action is already created and either insertAction or addAction is called. It is only inserted into the QMenu once.

QMenu::addMenu(const QString&) creates and appends the new QMenu that it returns. You are then inserting it a second time in the special case to move it to the same location as currently. Moving it in such a manner works on Windows and Linux (it moves it from the final position in the parent to the new location), but the comment in the Qt documentation suggests that may not work on MacOS.

My concern does not apply to the current implementation because the current implementation does not insert a QMenu (or QAction) into the same parent QMenu twice. It calls addAction *or* insertAction, for a given QAction (that is not already inserted in the parent Menu), not both. For QMenus, it only calls addMenu (because it doesn't have that case to insert in a specific position.)
ok, it's clear now, I see your point.

`insertMenu` only accepts QMenu as the second parameter:

`QAction * insertMenu(QAction *before, QMenu *menu)`

So to be able to use it, I need `QMenu * addMenu(const QString &title)` first and the result of that I can use for `insertMenu`.

Is there any other/better way to do this?

Note, the `addMenu()` will add it to the "default" section of Statistics which is the bottom part. And then I move it above `actionStatistics_REGISTER_STAT_GROUP_UNSORTED`. I am not moving to the same location.

The other way to do it would be to (in the insertMenu() case), use the `QMenu(const QString &title, QWidget *parent = nullptr)` constructor and then call insertMenu. It would probably be best to set the parent when doing that; the addMenu(const QString &title) convenience function automatically sets the parent - it's really just doing:

```
new_menu = QMenu(title, this);
this->addMenu(new_menu)
```

Yes, you're not moving it to the same location. It seems like it works on Linux and Windows, but I don't know if the behavior ("QMenus can only have a given child QMenu/QAction once, inserting a second time moves it to the new location") is guaranteed by Qt.
Updated.
